result.summary: Updates standardness policy in IsWitnessStandard to allow Taproot transactions with annexes, provided the annex is either marker-only (0x50) or unstructured data prefixed with 0x50 0x00. All non-P2A inputs in a transaction must include an annex if any input does, while native P2A inputs are exempt from opting in. Other annex prefixes remain non-standard, and annex weight is bounded only by the standard transaction weight limit.
result.problem: BIP 341 Taproot annexes are currently treated as non-standard by mempool policy, preventing nodes from relaying or accepting standard transactions that utilize annexes for arbitrary data or marker-based opt-in.
evidence: PR description: 'Builds on #27926 and Libre Relay' and 'This opt-in rule protects transactions that do not opt in. It does not prevent annex inflation by opted-in participants.'
Commit aa85bd97d1: 'Permit marker-only annexes and annexes whose first byte after the 0x50 marker is 0x00, reserving other prefixes for future semantics.'
result.changed_since_previous: Now provides the full patch including the P2A input exemption logic in IsWitnessStandard, unit tests in transaction_tests.cpp, and functional test coverage in feature_taproot.py.
result.card: Relaxes mempool policy to treat Taproot annexes as standard if they consist solely of the 0x50 marker or unstructured data starting with 0x50 0x00. Under current policy, any Taproot transaction with an annex is rejected from standard mempools. To protect multi-party transactions against unilateral witness inflation or pinning, the rule requires all non-P2A inputs in a transaction to include an annex if any input does. The PR revisits the concept from closed PR 27926 and Libre Relay without citing new external user requirements.

risk.why: Mistakes in standardness checks could permit standard relay of transactions exposed to pinning or witness inflation attacks, or lead to inconsistent relay policy across the network.
